description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by undergraduate or graduate level, sex, and race/ethnicity. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and enrollment level (EFFYLEV), with male, female, total, and nine race/ethnicity-category counts.

12-month instructional activity measured in total credit hours and/or contact hours for undergraduate and graduate activity. Records are reported by institution and instructional level, making this the table to query for instructional activity or the activity inputs used to derive 12-month FTE enrollment rather than student headcounts.

Institution-level academic library data for fiscal year 2019 (2019-20 coverage), including library characteristics, collections, expenditures, and services. The table covers degree-granting institutions; expenditure data are available only for institutions with total expenditures exceeding $100,000.

Institution-level data for the Fall 2019 undergraduate selection process for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking students, including admission considerations, applicants, admitted applicants, admitted students who enrolled, and SAT/ACT scores. The table applies only to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time students; SAT and ACT scores are reported only when test scores are required for admission. Each institution is represented by a single record, with admission-consideration response categories including “considered but not required” and no “do not know” option.

Awards and degrees conferred are counted by six-digit CIP program, first or second major, award level, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL, and includes total, male, and female awards overall and across nine race/ethnicity categories.

Students receiving any degree or certificate are counted by race/ethnicity and gender, without program or award-level detail. There is one record per institution, uniquely identified by UNITID, with total, male, and female recipient counts overall and across nine race/ethnicity categories.

Students receiving awards are counted by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age category. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age counts cover under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 and above, but race, gender, and age are not available in combination.

Programs offered and programs offered via distance education are counted by CIP program and award level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and CIPCODE: six-digit CIP records indicate which award levels are offered and offered via distance learning, two-digit CIP records summarize the six-digit programs in the CIP group, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals.
Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFLEVEL.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level, with separate measures for the nine race/ethnicity categories. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFALEVEL.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by distance-education status and student level, including exclusive distance-education enrollment by student location relative to the institution. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFDELEV.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID, EFBAGE, and LSTUDY. Age enrollment reporting is optional in even-numbered years; because 2019 is odd-numbered, this table has data for 2019.

Counts of first-time freshmen broken down by state of residence, including the number who graduated from high school the previous year. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFCSTATE. Residence enrollment reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2019 (odd) has data, subject to institution response.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, applicable only to institutions with undergraduate students. Only academic-year institutions report entering-class data, and institutions offering short programs of less than one year do not have retention data.

Institutional finance records for public institutions using GASB 34/35, with one record per institution and revenues by source, expenditures by functional and natural classification, endowments, assets, and liabilities. Detailed functional expenditures and the natural-classification categories for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are not available for fiscal year 2019.

Institutional finance records for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB, with one record per institution and revenues by source, expenditures by functional and natural classification, endowments, assets, and liabilities. Detailed functional expenditures and the natural-classification categories for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are not available for fiscal year 2019.

Institutional finance records for private for-profit institutions using FASB, with one record per institution and revenues by source, expenditures by functional and natural classification, assets, and liabilities. This table does not include endowment data; detailed functional expenditures and the natural-classification categories for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are not available for fiscal year 2019.

Graduation outcomes tracked through 200% of normal time for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at four-year and less-than-4-year institutions. Institution-by-graduation-status records are identified by UNITID and GRTYPE; four-year records cover bachelor’s completion, whereas less-than-4-year records cover completion of any degree or certificate, with outcomes shown at 100%, 150%, and 200% of normal time.

Graduation outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at four-year and two-year institutions, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Records are uniquely defined by UNITID and GRTYPE, which identifies the cohort and its graduation status; four-year records distinguish bachelor’s-seeking students from other degree/certificate-seeking students, while two-year records include transfer outcomes. Two-year institutions do not have 100%-of-normal-time completion counts by gender and race/ethnicity.

Graduation outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-2-year institutions, including enrollment and completion within 100% or 150% of normal time and transfer-out status. Records are institution-by-graduation-status observations identified by UNITID and GRTYPE, without the gender/race/ethnicity breakdown used in the broader institution table.

Graduation outcomes within 150% of normal time for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, separated into Pell recipients, subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell, and students who received neither aid type. Records are uniquely defined by UNITID and PSGRTYPE, the financial-aid subcohort and cohort/status type; four-year records distinguish bachelor’s-seeking from other degree/certificate-seeking students, while two-year and less-than-2-year records report overall completion outcomes.

Staff counts by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, faculty status, tenure status, and contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT, which defines the occupational and tenure-status category.

Full-time instructional-staff counts by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender, with contract-length detail for staff not on the tenure track. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT, combining faculty/tenure status with academic rank; coverage is limited to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years beginning in 2001, and became mandatory annually in 2016, so 2019 (odd) has data.

Full-time new hires by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender, with instructional new hires additionally classified by faculty/tenure status and contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT, which defines the primary occupation and instructional faculty/tenure category; the population is limited to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. For Fall 2019, new hires are permanent full-time hires made for the first time or after a break in service during November 1, 2018 through October 31, 2019, rather than the four-month window used in earlier tables. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years beginning in 2001, and became mandatory annually in 2016, so 2019 (odd) has data.

Full- and part-time staff counts by occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT, which combines occupational category with full- or part-time status. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years beginning in 2001, and became mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2019 (odd) has data.

Full-time instructional-staff counts by academic rank, faculty status, tenure status, and contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT; coverage is limited to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices.

Counts, salary outlays, average salaries, and equated nine-month salary measures for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by academic rank, gender, and number of months worked. Records are identified by UNITID and ARANK; counts are available for staff working fewer than nine months, but salary measures are not.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time nonmedical noninstructional staff by occupational category, recorded for each institution and occupational category.

Custom comparison-group membership records submitted for the 2020 Data Feedback Report, listing each comparison institution’s UNITID, name, and state. The row grain is a submitting institution–comparison-group–member-institution combination, with the submitting and member institution IDs and the comparison-group identifier defining the record.

Survey-component response and applicability records, including nonresponse imputation, parent/child or multiple-campus reporting, and revised-submission indicators. The row grain is one institution–survey-component combination, identified by UNITID and the survey component.

Institution directory records containing names, locations, contact and institutional URLs, active and Title IV participation status, control and level, highest award, and Carnegie classifications. The row grain is one record per institution, identified by UNITID.

Institution-level records on educational offerings, award levels, control and affiliations, admissions policy, distance education, special learning opportunities, library services, and athletic associations. The row grain is one institution, identified by UNITID; fields such as open admissions, distance education, and library services may reflect later winter or spring data collections.

Student charges and published cost-of-attendance amounts for full academic-year programs, including undergraduate, graduate, and selected professional-practice charges. The table is for institutions with primarily credit-hour academic programs using semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or another academic calendar, and the row grain is one institution identified by UNITID.

Student charges for vocational or occupational programs measured in clock hours or primarily in credit hours, including program counts and attendance costs for the largest program plus charges for up to five additional programs. The row grain is an institution–program record, identified by the institution and its program identifier.
Institution mission-statement records containing either the mission text or a web address for it. The row grain is one institution, identified by UNITID.

Award and enrollment outcomes for four entering undergraduate cohorts, split into eight unique subcohorts by first-time status, attendance intensity, and Pell-recipient status. It covers degree- and certificate-seeking undergraduates who entered degree-granting institutions from July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2012, with outcomes reported at four years (August 31, 2015), six years (August 31, 2017), and eight years (August 31, 2019); this 2019 table provides the eight-year status. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID) and cohort code (OMCHRT), and contains adjusted cohort size plus counts and percentages completing or still enrolled.

Student financial aid recipient counts, total aid dollars, and average aid dollars broken down by aid source and type for two populations: full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates and all undergraduates. The row grain is institution × student population × aid type/source, covering federal, Pell, other federal, state/local, institutional, and federal/nonfederal loan aid for the first population, and total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans for all undergraduates.

Average net price and the underlying financial-aid amounts for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in two groups: grant and scholarship recipients, and Title IV federal-aid recipients. The row grain is institution × population group; at public institutions, both groups are restricted to students paying in-district or in-state tuition.

Military servicemember and veterans-benefit recipient counts and total benefit dollars, broken down by student level—undergraduate versus graduate—and benefit type: Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits or Department of Defense Tuition Assistance. The row grain is institution × student level × benefit type; this collection is reported only in odd-numbered years, so 2019 (odd) has data.
